title: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General
description_short: Donald Trump uses Trump Foundation to bribe Florida Attorney General
description_medium: In 2013, the Trump Foundation sent $25,000 to a political group linked to Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi while her office was considering Trump University complaints. The foundation initially misreported the recipient, then corrected its tax filing, paid a $2,500 penalty and reimbursed itself. It acknowledged an illegal political contribution; the account does not establish a bribe or quid pro quo.
description_long: A 2016 Washington Post report said the Donald J. Trump Foundation paid $25,000 in 2013 to a political group connected to Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi while her office was considering fraud complaints involving Trump University. The foundation first reported the payment as a donation to a Kansas charity with a similar name; that charity did not receive the money. It later corrected its tax filing, paid a $2,500 penalty and reimbursed the foundation, according to a Trump Organization official. The foundation acknowledged that the payment was an illegal political contribution. Bondi’s office did not pursue the Trump University matter. This record establishes an improper campaign contribution and its timing alongside the office’s review of complaints. It does not establish that Trump paid Bondi personally, that she agreed to exchange official action for the donation, or that the contribution caused her office’s decision. “Bribe” asserts an exchange that the available account does not prove; the supported description is an illegal political contribution followed by a correction and penalty.

title: CDC and NIH Biomedical Research Destruction - $18 Billion Federal Science Elimination
description_short: CDC and NIH Biomedical Research Destruction - $18 Billion Federal Science Elimination
description_medium: Nature reported that NIH had terminated nearly 800 research projects by April 2025. A separate Science report described a proposed FY2026 NIH budget of $26.7 billion and reorganization that required congressional approval. The supplied sources do not establish an enacted $18 billion cut, a final NIH appropriation or the specific effects of changes to CDC programs.
description_long: Donald Trump systematically destroyed American biomedical research by cutting NIH funding from $47 billion to $28 billion while eliminating CDC's chronic disease prevention programs and terminating nearly 800 research projects that represented $2.3 billion in medical research designed to improve human health and lifespan. The comprehensive research destruction represented Trump's implementation of anti-science policies that prioritized budget reduction over medical advancement, forcing closure of research laboratories while terminating clinical trials and eliminating scientific programs that had historically advanced medical knowledge and saved American lives. The biomedical elimination included consolidating NIH's 27 institutes into 8 while abolishing nursing research, alternative medicine, minority health, and global health institutes that had addressed health disparities and provided medical research serving diverse populations and underserved communities. Trump's science destruction violated federal obligations to advance medical knowledge by eliminating research that had produced breakthrough treatments while forcing scientists to halt work on COVID-19, misinformation, and other health topics deemed 'problematic' by political appointees rather than scientific merit. The research termination created what scientists called 'sense of doom' among biomedical researchers who faced laboratory closures and career destruction while losing funding for projects that had scored highly during peer review but conflicted with administration ideology rather than scientific standards. The biomedical research destruction represented Project 2025's vision of science controlled by political ideology rather than scientific method, eliminating medical research that had historically improved public health while prioritizing political conformity over scientific advancement and medical breakthroughs that saved lives and reduced human suffering.
subcategory: Biomedical Research Elimination and Federal Science Destruction
organization_tags: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Donald Trump Jr. is paid $50,000 to meet with Russian assets in Paris
description_short: Donald Trump Jr. is paid $50,000 to meet with Russian assets in Paris
description_medium: According to the linked account, Donald Trump Jr. attended a private gathering of about 30 people at the Ritz in Paris in October 2016 and received at least $50,000. The Center for Political and Foreign Affairs hosted the event. The page attributes an intelligence connection to its organizers but supplies no payment record or underlying French assessment supporting its description of attendees as Russian assets.
description_long: The linked account says Donald Trump Jr. attended a private event of about 30 people at the Ritz Hotel in Paris in October 2016 and received at least $50,000. The Center for Political and Foreign Affairs hosted the gathering. The page identifies organizers Fabien Baussart and Randa Kassis and attributes ties to Russian officials to them. Kassis reportedly said she later discussed the meeting with Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Bogdanov and hoped a Trump victory would make cooperation with the United States over Syria possible. She also said she conveyed an idea through Trump Jr. These statements are attributed to an organizer; they do not establish that Trump Jr. delivered a policy proposal to his father or that any agreement resulted. The page calls participants Russian intelligence assets and attributes that description to French intelligence, but provides neither the assessment nor payment documentation. The available account supports a reported paid appearance and attributed follow-up contacts, not an independently verified intelligence meeting.
organization_tags: Center for Political and Foreign Affairs

title: Trump: State Dept. blocks autopsy results of Trump-Russia figure Vitaly Churkin
description_short: Trump: State Dept. blocks autopsy results of Trump-Russia figure Vitaly Churkin
description_medium: Vitaly Churkin, Russia’s ambassador to the United Nations, died in New York on February 20, 2017. The city medical examiner later did not release his autopsy results. The linked timeline alleges federal pressure and Russian objections but supplies no correspondence showing who requested withholding or under what authority. It also does not establish that Trump influenced the decision.
description_long: Vitaly Churkin, Russia’s ambassador to the United Nations, died in New York on February 20, 2017. The linked timeline says the city medical examiner initially needed toxicology results before determining the cause and later declined to release the autopsy findings. It alleges that federal officials asked New York City to withhold them and direct inquiries to the State Department, citing a legal obligation and Russia’s objection to disclosure. The timeline does not include letters or other independent records documenting that request, so the extent and legal basis of any federal role remain unverified. It also says Churkin met Donald Trump at a 1986 luncheon and later defended him at the United Nations. Those earlier contacts do not show that Trump influenced the medical examiner’s decision. The available account documents non-release and alleges federal pressure, but does not identify the decision-maker or controlling legal rule. Official correspondence or other records are needed to establish who sought withholding and whether that request affected the outcome.
organization_tags: New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner
